newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi to start registration for Clopidogrel.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi to start registration for Clopidogrel.

text.p: French drugs group Sanofi said on Wednesday it would start registration procedures for its Clopidrogel drug in the first quarter of 1997 following a positive clinical trial.

The company said that the results of the CAPRIE study of Clopidrogel had shown that the new drug was "significantly more effective than aspirin at reducing the likelihood of ischemic stroke, heart attack or vascular death in at-risk patients."
The study also showed that blood clots, or thrombi, in diseased blood vessels are a common link among some of the major fatal and disabling diseases of the industrialised world.
CAPRIE was a three-year randomised triple-blind international clinical study of 19,185 patients who had previously suffered an ischemic stroke, heart attack or claudication.
The results of the study were presented at the American Heart Association Meeting in New Orleans on Wednesday.
"This is a very great success for our research. We could not have hoped for a better result," Sanofi chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq told journalists in Paris.
Kurt Briner, chairman of Sanofi Pharma, said the company would start registration procedures in the United States and Europe in the first quarter of 1997.
He said it could take up to 12 months to obtain approval by the health authorities and between three to six months to set a price for the drug.

Copidogrel has been developed with Bristol-Myers Squibb of the United States under the terms of a 1993 agreement on cooperation on Copidrogrel and Irbestartan, for which registration has started in October.
The company gave no financial forecasts for sales of Clopidrogrel. Dehecq said that the potential for the drug was far superior to that of Ticlid, a leading Sanofi product.
Sanofi shares were suspended on Wednesday afternoon to await the results of the study. The shares will requote on Thursday.
Sanofi is majority-owned by oil group Elf-Aquitaine.
